title: Here, bhikkhus, a person has not attained internal serenity of mind and has not attained the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. That person, bhikkhus,…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a person has not attained internal serenity of mind and has not attained the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. That person, bhikkhus, should approach someone who has attained internal serenity of mind and the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena and say to him: 'Friend, how should the mind be established? How should the mind be settled? How should the mind be unified? How should the mind be concentrated? How should formations be seen? How should formations be known? How should formations be contemplated?' That person answers him: 'As has been seen, as has been known, thus, friend, should the mind be established; thus should the mind be settled; thus should the mind be unified; thus should the mind be concentrated; thus should formations be seen; thus should formations be known; thus should formations be contemplated.' After some time, that person attains internal serenity of mind and attains the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Then, bhikkhus, this person, after establishing himself in those wholesome states, should focus on training for the destruction of the taints.

title: Elder Cūḷagavaccha: A bhikkhu of great joy in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Buddha, Attains the peaceful state — the bliss of peace of all…
content:
Elder Cūḷagavaccha:

A bhikkhu of great joy in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Buddha,
Attains the peaceful state — the bliss of peace of all conditioned things.

title: These four things, bhikkhus, are true, not false, not otherwise. What four? 'This is suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the…
content: These four things, bhikkhus, are true, not false, not otherwise. What four? 'This is suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the origin of suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the cessation of suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. These four things, bhikkhus, are true, not false, not otherwise. Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is suffering.' ... an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

title: Almsfood, lodging, a place to sit, water for washing, And the outer robe — after hearing the Dhamma taught by the Well-Gone One, A wise…
content:
Almsfood, lodging, a place to sit, water for washing,
And the outer robe — after hearing the Dhamma taught by the Well-Gone One,
A wise disciple, having reflected, should use them.

Therefore, almsfood, lodging, water for washing, and the outer robe —
Do not become attached to these things.
A bhikkhu, like a water drop on a lotus leaf, should not cling.

title: Elder Jotidāsa: Those who use ropes, who rob in various ways, Those cruel people who harm others — Thus they cause harm, because kamma does…
content:
Elder Jotidāsa:

Those who use ropes, who rob in various ways,
Those cruel people who harm others —
Thus they cause harm, because kamma does not vanish.

Whatever kamma one does, good or evil,
One is the heir of that kamma, of the kamma one is doing.

title: And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not fumigate? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not teach the Dhamma extensively to others as he has heard and…
content: And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not fumigate? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not teach the Dhamma extensively to others as he has heard and learned it. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu who does not fumigate. And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not know the ford? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not from time to time approach those bhikkhus who are learned, who have received the tradition of the scriptures, who are experts in the Dhamma, experts in the Discipline, experts in the summaries; he does not ask them, does not question them: 'How is this, venerable sir? What is the meaning of this?' Those venerable ones do not reveal what is unrevealed, do not clarify what is unclear, and regarding various points of Dhamma, they do not remove doubt. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu who does not know the ford. And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not know the drinking place? Here, bhikkhus, when the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata is being taught, he does not attain the meaning of faith, the Dhamma of faith, does not attain gladness connected with the Dhamma. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu who does not know the drinking place.

title: Truly, bhikkhus, whoever with evil intent looks at animals that are being killed, being led to slaughter — because of that, he is not fit…
content: Truly, bhikkhus, whoever with evil intent looks at animals that are being killed, being led to slaughter — because of that, he is not fit to ride an elephant, not fit to ride a horse, not fit to ride a chariot, not fit to ride a carriage, not fit to enjoy wealth, or not fit to live among great or heaped-up wealth. What to say of one who with evil intent looks at human beings who are being killed, being led to slaughter! Truly, bhikkhus, it is for his long-term harm and suffering that, after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is worth being a friend. What five? He does not tell to do farm work; does not delight…
content: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is worth being a friend. What five? He does not tell to do farm work; does not delight in litigation; does not oppose the leading bhikkhus; does not live a purposeless life, prolonging it thus; is able from time to time to expound, encourage, inspire, and delight with a Dhamma talk. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is worth being a friend.

title: Bhikkhus, I say that killing living beings is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that taking…
content: Bhikkhus, I say that killing living beings is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that taking what is not given is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that sexual misconduct is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that false speech is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that divisive speech is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that harsh speech is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that idle chatter is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that covetousness is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that ill-will is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that wrong view is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Thus, bhikkhus, greed is a cause for the origination of action, hatred is a cause for the origination of action, delusion is a cause for the origination of action. With the cessation of greed comes the cessation of action, with the cessation of hatred comes the cessation of action, with the cessation of delusion comes the cessation of action.

title: A giver of a meal, bhikkhus, a donor, gives five things to the recipient. What five? He gives life, gives beauty, gives happiness, gives strength,…
content: A giver of a meal, bhikkhus, a donor, gives five things to the recipient. What five? He gives life, gives beauty, gives happiness, gives strength, gives eloquence. Giving life, he has a share in life, whether celestial or human. Giving beauty, he has a share in beauty, whether celestial or human. Giving happiness, he has a share in happiness, whether celestial or human. Giving strength, he has a share in strength, whether celestial or human. Giving eloquence, he has a share in eloquence, whether celestial or human. A giver of a meal, bhikkhus, a donor, gives these five things to the recipient.
